## What this step does

Mortality Step 3 reads the classified Step 2 dataset, calculates the approved mortality burden measures and creates the private staging package.

It creates exact private values. It does not apply the final public disclosure-control candidate, approve a release, copy files to the public repository or link DCO events.

## Input

`$BNR_DATA_DERIVED/mortality/yYYYY/mMM/bnr_mort_s2_YYYYMM.dta`

The selected year/month identifies the **data freeze**. Step 3 derives the analysis period separately. The current dashboard series begins in 2010 and Step 3 includes completed calendar years only.

## Published reporting structure prepared by Step 3

The staged release contains three metric IDs:

| Metric | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `MORT-BURDEN-001` | Mortality counts and approved rolling-comparator rows |
| `MORT-BURDEN-002` | Annual percentage distributions |
| `MORT-RATE-001` | Annual crude and directly age-standardised mortality rates per 100,000 |

Both Primary and Inclusive mortality definitions are carried through the reporting lattice.

`MORT-RATE-001` is annual only: All CVD, Heart and Stroke; both sexes, women
and men; and crude/all-age plus directly age-standardised forms. It uses the
approved private UN WPP 2024 Barbados denominator asset and fixed WHO World
Standard Population. Step 3 also supplies 95% statistical CIs (Garwood for
crude rates; Fay-Feuer gamma for ASRs). The dashboard must display supplied
rows only; it must never calculate a rate or CI.

The public monthly scope is deliberately restricted to All CVD, both sexes, all ages and monthly count. Quarterly and annual rows contain the additional approved event-type and sex detail; annual All-CVD rows also contain the approved broad age groups.

## Run Step 3

1. In Stata, choose **User > BNR > Update mortality dashboard > Step 3: Build mortality burden data**.
2. Enter the Step 2 release year and month.
3. Leave replacement unticked for a first run.
4. Run the step.
5. Confirm the summary reports `Completed successfully`.
6. Check the reported analysis years and metric row counts.
7. Open the staging package and confirm the datasets, metadata and review material are present.
8. Do not treat the suppression-review workbook as the Step 4 human review package. Step 4 owns the public-candidate disclosure control and review materials.

## Outputs

The package is staged under:

`$BNR_STAGING/mortality/burden/mort_YYYY_MM/`

| Output | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `datasets/mort_burden_metrics_mort_YYYY_MM.dta` and `.csv` | Exact private release-stamped burden data. |
| `datasets/mort_burden_metrics_current.dta` and `.csv` | Exact private stable-name copies for the selected staging package. |
| `metadata/mort_burden_package.yml` | Package identity, scope and provenance. |
| `review/mort_burden_qa_mort_YYYY_MM.csv` | Automated calculation/staging QA. |
| `review/mort_burden_suppression_review_mort_YYYY_MM.csv` and `.xlsx` | Step 3 disclosure worklist feeding Step 4. |
| `readme.txt` | Short private package guide. |
| Step 3 log | Private operational record under `$BNR_PRIVATE_LOGS/`. |

Do not edit any generated package file.

Step 4 applies rate protection only as a secondary companion to a protected
matching annual death count. Rate rows do not create additional count
suppression decisions.

## Command-line equivalent

```stata
do "$BNR_STATA/mortality/bnr_mort_s3_burden.do" 2026 7
```

Use `replace` only for a deliberate rebuild. The optional `debug` word exposes detailed child-script output for development/troubleshooting and is not needed in routine use.

## If Step 3 does not complete

Check that the matching Step 2 DTA exists and that the selected release produces the expected completed-year analysis range. Read the private log before authorising replacement.
